places.n: Church of the Nativity of the Blessed Virgin Mary
places.ad: 1259 Upper Serangoon Road, Singapore 534795
places.w: A National Monument (gazetted 14 Jan 2005) and the historic heart of Serangoon's Teochew Catholic community, which was mostly farmers in the 19th century. The present Gothic church — pointed arches, a soaring nave — was blessed on 8 Dec 1901 and restored in 2019; the mission dates to pioneer priest Fr Ambrose Maistre in 1852.
places.k: Free entry; a stop on the Hougang Heritage Trail

places.n: Hougang Tou Mu Kung (Kew Ong Yah Temple)
places.ad: 779A Upper Serangoon Road, Singapore
places.w: Singapore's oldest temple dedicated to the Nine Emperor Gods (Kew Ong Yah), completed 1921 and gazetted a National Monument on 14 Jan 2005. Its blend of Hokkien and later Teochew roof forms anchors Hougang's Teochew heritage, and it remains the focus of the annual Nine Emperor Gods Festival.
places.k: Free entry; busiest during the ninth-lunar-month festival

places.ad: 20 Kensington Park Road, Singapore 557269
places.w: Serangoon Gardens' legendary supper hawker centre, open since 1972 with around 36 stalls. A night-time institution for BBQ stingray and sotong, Hokkien mee, satay, satay bee hoon, orh luak and charcoal chicken wings — as much a neighbourhood landmark as an eating spot.
places.k: Evenings to late night; busiest for supper

places.ad: Serangoon Garden Circus (Serangoon Garden Way / Kensington Park Road), Singapore
places.w: One of Singapore's oldest private landed estates, laid out in the 1950s by British developer Steven Charles Macey to house British, Australian and NZ servicemen from the nearby RAF Chia Keng camp — which is why nearly every street bears a British name. The Circus roundabout is its social heart, ringed by Chomp Chomp, the market and myVillage.

places.ad: Upper Serangoon Road (trail markers near Kovan MRT), Singapore
places.w: NHB's self-guided trail through 'Au Kang' — one of Singapore's oldest heartland towns and a historic Teochew enclave. Eighteen sites across three routes ('Landmarks of Hougang', 'Institutions of Service', 'Architectural Gems'), and the first heartland trail to include two National Monuments (Church of the Nativity and Tou Mu Kung).

places.ad: Hougang Avenue 8 (junction of Hougang Ave 8 & Ave 10), Singapore
places.w: A 16-hectare Hougang park built around a 5-hectare lake — a former sand quarry once used to reclaim the area's swamps. Popular for lakeside jogging, fishing decks and a heron-frequented waterfront, and a green anchor of the Hougang edge.

places.ad: 1 Maju Avenue, Singapore 556679
places.w: The neighbourhood mall on the site of the old Serangoon Garden Village and its 1950s Paramount Theatre (demolished 2009). Pitched as a 'village' concept mall, it keeps the Circus area's daily rhythm going with a supermarket, eateries and services.

places.n: Montfort Schools (formerly Holy Innocents' English School)
places.ad: Montfort Secondary School, 50 Hougang Avenue 8, Singapore 538785
places.w: Founded in 1916 as Holy Innocents' English School beside the Church of the Nativity by the parish priest of Serangoon, renamed Montfort in 1959 and run by the Gabrielite Brothers. A cornerstone of Hougang's 'Holy Land' cluster of Catholic institutions; a heritage gallery traces its founding.
places.k: Active school; grounds not open to visitors

places.ad: Upper Serangoon Road (former 5th milestone), Kovan, Singapore
places.w: A Hougang Heritage Trail marker recalling Lim Tua Tow market at the old 5th milestone of Upper Serangoon Road — for decades the marketplace that served the population of Singapore's north-eastern region before the town was redeveloped.

places.ad: 33 Yio Chu Kang Road, Singapore 545677
places.w: The community stadium and adjoining sport centre serving the Serangoon–Hougang belt — running track, stands, gym and pool. A neighbourhood recreation hub on the western edge of the district.
places.k: ActiveSG facility; public sessions & fees apply

places.ad: 23 Serangoon Central, Singapore 556083
places.w: The North-East's biggest mall (opened 2011), integrated with Serangoon MRT (NEL/Circle Line interchange) and the air-conditioned bus interchange. The regional shopping-and-transit anchor on the western edge of the Upper Serangoon district, with a rooftop dog run and garden.

places.ad: 2 Hillside Drive, Singapore 548920
places.w: The oldest mosque in Hougang, built in 1921 on land donated by Gujarati merchant-philanthropist Ahmad Mohamed Salleh Angullia to serve the area's Muslim community of farmers and traders. A stop on the Hougang Heritage Trail, just off Upper Serangoon Road near Kovan.
places.k: Active mosque; visitors welcome outside prayer times

places.ad: 62 Hougang Avenue 3, Singapore 538844
places.w: Completed in 1987 and designed by Tay Kheng Soon of Akitek Tenggara, this is widely regarded as Singapore's first truly modernist Chinese temple — its roof rising in eight-sided prisms that evoke a lotus, its corners deliberately kept un-sharp on the deities' guidance. A Hougang Heritage Trail 'Architectural Gem' and a documented modern-movement building.

places.n: Church of St Vincent de Paul
places.ad: 301 Yio Chu Kang Road, Singapore 805910
places.w: A Catholic parish on Kovan's western edge whose roots trace to 1959, when Fr Henri Saussard began ministering to the rubber tappers, fishermen and farmers of the Jalan Kayu area; the present church was blessed and opened at Christmas 1970. It continues to serve the north-eastern Catholic community around Serangoon Gardens and Kovan.
places.k: Active parish; Mass times on the church site

places.ad: 7 Lorong Buangkok (off Gerald Drive, via Buangkok Crescent), Singapore 547557
places.w: Singapore's last surviving mainland village, established in 1956 when traditional-medicine seller Sng Teow Koon bought the swampy land and rented plots to Malay and Chinese families. A cluster of zinc-roofed houses on dirt tracks around a surau, in the Trafalgar (Buangkok) subzone of Hougang; Ms Sng Mui Hong, the founder's youngest daughter, still lives here as landlord. Old four-digit street signs survive.
places.k: Free; a living village — visit respectfully, don't enter homes

places.ad: Lorong Halus Wetland, Lorong Halus North (eastern bank of Serangoon Reservoir), Singapore
places.w: An 18-football-field wetland on the Hougang/Defu edge — a former landfill transformed into a natural water-treatment site whose cattails bio-remediate rainwater before it enters the adjoining Serangoon Reservoir. Bounded by Kangkar to the west and Defu Industrial Park to the south, it's a family recreation spot reached over the red steel-railway-style Lorong Halus Bridge from Punggol Promenade.
places.k: Open daily, free; cycling, fishing decks & birdwatching

places.ad: 5 Lorong Low Koon, Singapore 536451
places.w: One of Singapore's first Chinese mission schools, founded in 1892 as Tao Nan School in the Upper Serangoon village and renamed Holy Innocents' Chinese Boys' School in 1920 under Fr Becheras. Part of Hougang's 'Holy Land' cluster of Catholic institutions around the Church of the Nativity; the school returned to a rebuilt Hougang campus, blessed by Archbishop Nicholas Chia in 2006.
places.k: Active school; grounds not open to visitors

places.ad: 56 Hougang Avenue 3, Singapore 538842
places.w: A Taoist temple complex completed in 1996 and a Hougang Heritage Trail 'Architectural Gems' landmark. It houses three older temples — Kai Hock Tong, Keat Sun Beo and Chao Ying Kong — relocated and consolidated from their original sites at Wolskel Road, Lorong Chuan and Yishun, a common Singapore story of temples resettled by redevelopment.

places.ad: Chomp Chomp Food Centre, 20 Kensington Park Road, S557269
places.w: A Michelin Plate stall and Chomp Chomp's most famous name — thick yellow noodles and bee hoon fried with prawns and squid in a prawn stock simmered for hours, finished with a dollop of sambal. The go-to plate at Serangoon Gardens' legendary supper hawker centre.

places.ad: Chomp Chomp Food Centre, 20 Kensington Park Road, S557269
places.w: One of two Chomp Chomp stalls listed in the MICHELIN Guide with a Michelin Plate — skewers grilled over charcoal to order, a supper-time institution best eaten late at Serangoon Gardens with a plate of BBQ chicken wings alongside.

places.ad: Chomp Chomp Food Centre, 20 Kensington Park Road, S557269
places.w: The standout orh luak of Chomp Chomp — eggs and starch fried until charred and crisp at the edges around plump, briny oysters, drizzled with tangy chilli. A perennial pick across the centre's food-guide round-ups.

places.ad: Chomp Chomp Food Centre, #01-29, 20 Kensington Park Road, S557269
places.w: Chicken wings are practically Chomp Chomp's mascot, and Good Luck (Stall 29) grills some of the most sought-after — burnished, charred-edged skin over juicy meat, at roughly S$1.30 a wing. A supper staple of the Serangoon Gardens crowd.

places.ad: Chomp Chomp Food Centre, 20 Kensington Park Road, S557269
places.w: Chomp Chomp's best sambal BBQ seafood — fresh, flaky stingray blanketed in an addictive sambal and grilled on a banana leaf (from S$12 for a small), plus BBQ sotong and cockles. A late-night favourite that draws its own queue.

places.n: Ang Sar Lee Satay Bee Hoon
places.ad: Chomp Chomp Food Centre, 20 Kensington Park Road, S557269
places.w: A 40-plus-year Chomp Chomp veteran plating thin bee hoon drowned in a fragrant satay peanut gravy with cuttlefish, prawns, pork and tau pok — the Serangoon Gardens rendition of a dish few hawkers still make well.

places.ad: Chomp Chomp Food Centre, 20 Kensington Park Road, S557269
places.w: The other half of Chomp Chomp's Hokkien mee debate — a darker, wetter plate with its own loyal supporters who rate it over Ah Hock. Between the two, Serangoon Gardens arguably has Singapore's densest Hokkien mee rivalry.

places.ad: Serangoon Garden Market & Food Centre, 49A Serangoon Garden Way, S555945
places.w: The most-recommended stall in the market — a Muslim-owned nasi lemak (from S$3) built on freshly squeezed coconut milk, pandan-scented rice and a shiok sambal, with crisp ikan bilis and add-ons. Serangoon Gardens' daytime counterpoint to Chomp Chomp.

places.ad: Serangoon Garden Market & Food Centre, #01-44, 49A Serangoon Garden Way, S555945
places.w: Rated among Singapore's best Teochew braised duck — tender, herbal braised duck over rice (from S$4) with pig's stomach soup and offal, from a decades-old recipe. Queues form before it opens.

places.ad: Serangoon Garden Market & Food Centre, #01-21, 49A Serangoon Garden Way, S555945
places.w: A long-running kway chap stall (formerly Blanco Court) ladling silky flat rice sheets in braising liquor with well-stewed Teochew pig offal, braised egg and tau pok — a market breakfast institution.

places.ad: Serangoon Garden Market & Food Centre, 49A Serangoon Garden Way, S555945
places.w: A market favourite for old-school roasted and poached Hainanese chicken rice, repeatedly singled out across the Serangoon Garden Market food-guide round-ups.

places.ad: Serangoon Garden Market & Food Centre, #01-45/46, 49A Serangoon Garden Way, S555945
places.w: A 40-year neighbourhood bakery baking from 2am — classic coconut, cream-puff, chicken-sausage and curry buns from S$1.10, all made from scratch. A generational fixture inside the market.

places.ad: Serangoon Garden Market & Food Centre, 49A Serangoon Garden Way, S555945
places.w: A veteran orh luak stall frying crisp, starchy oyster omelettes to order — one of the market's most-named stalls in the food-guide coverage of Serangoon Garden.

places.n: Lao Song Fa (Botanical Garden Famous Fishball Noodle)
places.ad: Serangoon Garden Market & Food Centre, 49A Serangoon Garden Way, S555945
places.w: An old-name fishball noodle stall carrying the 'Botanical Garden Famous' lineage — springy mee pok tossed with handmade fishballs, fishcake and minced pork, a market staple for decades.

places.ad: Serangoon Garden Market & Food Centre, 49A Serangoon Garden Way, S555945
places.w: A market prawn-noodle mainstay, its rich prawn-and-pork broth a recurring recommendation in the Serangoon Garden Market guides.

places.ad: Serangoon Garden Market & Food Centre, Stall 12, 49A Serangoon Garden Way, S555945
places.w: An old-school snack stall for hum ji beng, traditional pastries and kueh — the kind of nostalgic bite the Serangoon Garden Market food guides keep flagging.

places.ad: Serangoon Garden Market & Food Centre, #01-25, 49A Serangoon Garden Way, S555945
places.w: A long-standing stall for min jiang kueh (folded peanut pancake) and hum ji beng (from about S$1.30) — a market breakfast and tea-time regular.

places.ad: Kovan 209 Market & Food Centre, #01-17, 209 Hougang Street 21, S530209
places.w: A decades-old stall hand-making Teochew kueh — soon kueh, png kueh and gu chye kueh at around S$1 each, using only fresh fillings. A Kovan 209 heritage name.

places.ad: Kovan 209 Market & Food Centre, #01-25, 209 Hougang Street 21, S530209
places.w: The lunch-hour queue of Kovan 209 — a heaped plate of Hainanese-style chye png flooded with curry, braise and pork gravies, with fried pork chop and cabbage. Old-school comfort food.

places.ad: Kovan 209 Market & Food Centre, #01-30, 209 Hougang Street 21, S530209
places.w: A three-in-one stall doing moist, well-coated Hokkien mee in a velvety prawn stock (about S$3.50), plus fried oyster and white/black carrot cake with eggy bits and preserved radish.

places.ad: Kovan 209 Market & Food Centre, #01-57, 209 Hougang Street 21, S530209
places.w: A decades-old wanton mee stall with a constant queue for simple, honest bowls of springy noodles in soy sauce with char siew and wantons.

places.ad: Kovan 209 Market & Food Centre, 209 Hougang Street 21, S530209
places.w: A community-loved wanton mee for its well-charred char siew and springy egg noodles — one of Kovan 209's most cited noodle stalls.

places.ad: Kovan 209 Market & Food Centre, 209 Hougang Street 21, S530209
places.w: Fishball noodles with a choice of dry, soup or a coconutty, mildly spicy laksa broth, topped with fishcake, minced meat and braised mushroom — a Kovan 209 regular.

places.ad: 59 Serangoon Garden Way, S555955
places.w: A Serangoon Gardens institution since 1983 — the Hainanese founders opened a chicken rice stall, then hired a Nonya chef, and today it is rated among Singapore's best traditional Hainanese chicken rice with a Peranakan zi char spread.

places.ad: 1 Kensington Park Road, S557253
places.w: The 24-hour prata and mamak institution of Serangoon Gardens, famed for crispy plain prata, the over-the-top 'roti tsunami', chocolate prata and maggi mee goreng — its R.K. Special once a Sunday Times 'Cheap & Good' pick.

places.ad: 56 Serangoon Garden Way, S555952
places.w: A 24-hour prata house that gave R.K. its cross-street rival — prata, murtabak and maggi goreng served with massive drink towers, a Serangoon Gardens supper staple.

places.ad: 65 Serangoon Garden Way, S555961
places.w: A long-running Serangoon Gardens cafe from the Atlas Coffeehouse / Columbus Coffee team — minimalist interiors, a solid brunch menu and a cult dark-chocolate-and-miso-caramel softserve. The area's flagship specialty-coffee address.

places.n: Tian Wai Tian Fish Head Steamboat
places.ad: 203 Hougang Street 21, #01-89, S530203
places.w: A tiny, wildly popular Kovan streetside zi char serving Teochew-style fish head steamboat in traditional charcoal aluminium pots — pomfret, red grouper or bighead carp — plus salted-egg pork ribs and prawn-paste chicken. Usually packed out by 5.30pm.

places.ad: 965 Upper Serangoon Road, S534721
places.w: The perennial after-midnight queue on Upper Serangoon Road is a Kovan landmark in itself. Founded 1979 (by the eldest of the Koh nasi lemak family), it's iconic for Chinese-style coconut rice with super-crispy chicken wings, luncheon meat and fried egg.

places.ad: 945 Upper Serangoon Road, S534711
places.w: A Kovan casual restaurant doing a distinctive Thai take on kway chap — a light, peppery broth (milder than bak kut teh) with silky, curled rice sheets and Thai-style braised sides, open till 3am for the supper crowd.

places.ad: 957 Upper Serangoon Road, S534717
places.w: A late-night Kovan dessert cafe open until 2am, pairing crisp waffles with handcrafted ice cream in offbeat flavours — a viral-friendly stop on the Upper Serangoon supper strip.

places.ad: Hougang Village, 681 Hougang Avenue 8, #01-855, S530681
places.w: The mainstay 24/7 mamak for Kovan and Hougang residents — plain prata about S$2.60 for two, egg prata, murtabak and teh tarik at any hour. A Hougang-edge supper anchor.

places.ad: Space @ Kovan, 9 Yio Chu Kang Road, #01-54, S545523
places.w: An artisanal bakery-cafe on the Kovan edge known for freshly baked sourdough, baguettes and a viral salted-caramel cube croissant — a modern counterpoint to the neighbourhood's old-school bakes.

places.ad: 730 Upper Serangoon Road, #01-01, Singapore
places.w: A well-loved Kovan brunch cafe for specialty coffee and toasted jaffles in a light, plant-filled space — it closed on 19 Jan 2025. Kept here as a flagged closure.

places.n: Seng Kee Mushroom Minced Meat Noodle
places.ad: Serangoon Garden Market & Food Centre, #01-36, 49A Serangoon Garden Way, S555945
places.w: A 40-plus-year mushroom minced-meat noodle stall — dry mee pok balanced with a house chilli, deep slow-braised mushroom sauce and crispy pork lard, plus a fish-maw soup its regulars swear by. One of Serangoon Garden Market's most cited names.

places.ad: Chomp Chomp Food Centre, #01-12, 20 Kensington Park Road, S557269
places.w: A humble 50-year wanton mee tucked in a back corner of Chomp Chomp (no relation to the bakery of the same name) — springy noodles, silky-skinned wantons and char siew all made in-house, in a broth with robust ikan-bilis notes.

places.n: Wang Da Shen Chicken Wing & Satay
places.ad: Chomp Chomp Food Centre, 20 Kensington Park Road, S557269
places.w: One of Chomp Chomp's newer stalls (opened during the pandemic) and the only one that stays open till 2am — charcoal-grilled chicken wings and satay for the deep-supper crowd at Serangoon Gardens.

places.n: Fa Ji Minced Meat Fishball Noodle
places.ad: Kovan 209 Market & Food Centre, #01-05, 209 Hougang Street 21, S530209
places.w: The most popular of Kovan 209's three fishball-noodle stalls — springy noodles tossed with handmade fishballs, fishcake and minced pork, a heartland breakfast regular.

places.ad: Kovan 209 Market & Food Centre, #01-53, 209 Hougang Street 21, S530209
places.w: Kovan 209's go-to Malay-Muslim stall — nasi lemak sets alongside hawker staples like mee rebus, mee siam, lontong and soto, the halal anchor of the food centre.

places.ad: Block 212 Hougang Street 21, #01-333, S530212
places.w: The Kovan branch of homegrown gelateria Tom's Palette, opened March 2024 and open till midnight, known for adventurous flavours and a putu-mayam-topped cone nodding to the area's coconut-plantation past. Honest note: after 21 years, both Tom's Palette outlets are set to close in October 2026.

places.ad: 5 Simon Road, S545893
places.w: A Kovan brunch stalwart a short walk from the MRT and one of the few dog-friendly cafes in the area — hearty brunch plates, truffle linguine and desserts like the oozy goma black-sesame tart and Lola's chocolate cake.

places.ad: Block 211 Hougang Street 21, #01-291, S530211
places.w: A minimalist neighbourhood cafe in Kovan serving a focused menu of Korean-leaning fusion food, bingsu desserts and hand-crafted beverages — a modern counterpoint to the estate's old-school stalls.

places.ad: 80A Serangoon Garden Way, Singapore
places.w: A Serangoon Gardens dessert institution on the second floor of a shophouse — famous for its trademarked durian mousse served on ice with a dollop of durian flesh, one of 50-plus traditional Chinese desserts.

places.ad: myVillage @ Serangoon Garden, #02-01, 1 Maju Avenue, S556679
places.w: A family-style Cantonese-Teochew restaurant at myVillage helmed by ex-Lei Garden head chef Tony Wong (40-plus years, credited as the original creator of mango sago with pomelo) — hearty zi char and a full dim sum spread.

places.ad: 943 Upper Serangoon Road, Singapore
places.w: A KL-style chilli ban mian in an Upper Serangoon Road coffee shop, open into the small hours — al-dente noodles with minced pork, ikan bilis, fried shallots, a runny egg and a fierce dried-shrimp chilli that draws the supper crowd.

places.ad: Block 212 Hougang Street 21, #01-341, S530212
places.w: The pioneer of affordable neighbourhood Thai in Kovan (since 2008), the most popular eatery on Hougang Street 21 — a near-constant queue for pandan chicken, green curry, mango salad and pineapple fried rice at hawker prices.

places.ad: 203 Hougang Street 21, #01-45, S530203
places.w: A family-run Kovan zi char eatery famed for its fragrant curry fish head, otah and the home-style dishes the family fancies — a low-key neighbourhood favourite off Hougang Street 21.

places.ad: 685 Hougang Street 61, #01-150, S530685
places.w: A Hougang corner-stall congee institution with a perpetual 30-minute queue — thick, hearty bowls of smooth Cantonese-style porridge piled with generous ingredients, warming Hougang residents for decades.

places.ad: 756 Upper Serangoon Road, #01-15/16 Upper Serangoon Shopping Centre, S534626
places.w: An authentic family-run Teochew restaurant on Upper Serangoon Road — steamed fish, braised goose and duck, oyster omelette and the mui-and-porridge classics — a fitting anchor for the district's Teochew ('Au Kang') heritage.

places.ad: Ci Yuan Hawker Centre, 51 Hougang Avenue 9, #01-40, Singapore 538776
places.w: A MICHELIN Guide-listed stall that pairs fragrant coconut rice with Ayam Taliwang, the fiery Lombok-style grilled chicken — the smoky, chilli-slicked bird against the cool creamy rice. The Ci Yuan branch of a beloved north-east name, right in Hougang.

places.ad: Hainanese Village Centre, 105 Hougang Avenue 1, #02-01, Singapore 530105
places.w: One of Singapore's best Teochew braised duck rice stalls, tucked in Hougang's Hainanese Village Centre (Lorong Ah Soo). Tender lean duck over yam rice, drenched in a mildly sweet-savoury five-spice sauce, with an anchovy-loaded sambal. Opens at dawn and usually sells out by early lunch.

places.ad: Kovan 209 Market & Food Centre, 209 Hougang Street 21, #01-66, Singapore 530209
places.w: Third- and fourth-generation hawkers who have fried their wet-style Hokkien mee to the same recipe since 1960 — whole prawns, squid rings and pork belly over noodles and bee hoon fried dry so they drink up a prawn-head-and-pork-rib stock, with free-flow crispy lard. Named for its old Simon Road home, now relocated to Kovan 209.

places.ad: 174C Hougang Avenue 1, Singapore 533174
places.w: Widely cited as Singapore's best-rated fish soup — a clean, refined broth from a couple who started at Zion Road Blk 91 in 2002 before landing under a quiet Hougang coffeeshop. The 'hei bai' bowl of fried and sliced fish together, done with milk, is the order.

places.n: Hougang Oyster Omelette & Fried Kway Teow
places.ad: Blk 435A Hougang Avenue 8, Singapore 531435
places.w: A 30-year Hougang heritage stall run by Mr and Mrs Ong that still fries its oyster omelette in pork lard, with big juicy oysters and a fragrant char kway teow alongside. One of the island's best-rated orh luak, worth the queue.

places.ad: Kovan 209 Market & Food Centre, 209 Hougang Street 21, #01-37, Singapore 530209
places.w: A Kovan 209 Hokkien mee stall run by the former cook of Teow Heng Cooked Food. A big plate of thick and thin noodles with prawns, cuttlefish and pork lard in a seafood broth, fried with wok hei to spare — the 'Davis Prawn Noodles' are the house signature.

places.ad: 1022 Upper Serangoon Road, Singapore 534760
places.w: A roadside Upper Serangoon stall within walking distance of Kovan MRT, packed each morning for handmade Teochew kueh — soon kueh, png kueh — bursting with well-seasoned fillings and made fresh daily.

places.ad: 684 Hougang Avenue 8, #01-953, Singapore 530684
places.w: An under-HDB dessert cafe by an Italy-trained gelato-maker who won the Singapore Gelato Championship in 2019 ('Singapore's Best Gelato') with a Pear, Ginger and Ginger Flower scoop inspired by his father's Chinese rojak. The Hougang outlet opened January 2023.

places.ad: Hainanese Village Centre, 105 Hougang Avenue 1, #02-37, Singapore 530105
places.w: A hidden gem at Hainanese Village Centre serving just two dishes — fried Hokkien prawn mee and char kway teow — with almost everything made from scratch: the prawn stock, pork lard, chilli, even hand-peeled garlic. Run by Mrs Lu and her husband for over a decade.

places.ad: Hainanese Village Centre, 105 Hougang Avenue 1, #02-30, Singapore 530105
places.w: The First Class Fragrance nasi lemak — by queue, the most popular stall in the whole of Hainanese Village Centre. Fragrant coconut rice with crispy fried fish fillet, ikan selar, whitebait and sambal for a few dollars; regularly sold out before its stated noon close.

places.ad: Hainanese Village Centre, 105 Hougang Avenue 1, #02-32, Singapore 530105
places.w: A 30-year hawker Western stall at Hainanese Village Centre — crispy-outside, tender-inside chicken cutlet, chicken chop, pork chop and fish & chips. Old-school flame-grilled plates at hawker prices.

places.ad: Blk 211 Hougang Street 21, #01-285, Singapore 530211
places.w: Billed as Singapore's first heartland izakaya — a 'standing bar' under an HDB block in Kovan serving good Japanese street food late into the night (till 2am on Saturdays). A neighbourhood spot for a late plate and a drink.

places.n: Lorong Ah Soo Lor Mee (Fu Yuan Mei Shi)
places.ad: Hainanese Village Centre, 105 Hougang Avenue 1, #02-36, Singapore 530105
places.w: A long-loved Hainanese Village Centre stall drawing crowds for its lor mee — flat noodles under a luscious thick gravy with a secret ingredient — and laksa. A Hougang breakfast-crowd fixture.

places.ad: 682 Hougang Avenue 4, Singapore 530682
places.w: A humble coffeeshop stall turning out old-school min jiang kueh (Chinese pancakes) far bigger and more generously stuffed than most — red bean, yam, black sesame, matcha, peanut, chocolate — at S$1.30-1.60 a piece. Instagram-famous, and sells out.

places.ad: 377 Hougang Street 32, #01-32, Hougang Rivercourt, Singapore 530377
places.w: A Hougang dessert bakery known for inventive sweets — Korean-French Fatcarons (fat macarons), viral cookie-croissants, mochi cakes and durian cakes. A modern sugar stop in the heartland.

places.ad: Ci Yuan Hawker Centre, 51 Hougang Avenue 9, #01-18, Singapore 538776
places.w: A Korean-owned hawker stall at Ci Yuan turning out legit Korean fried chicken — crackly-crisp, in flavours like honey butter — from around S$6.50. Hawker-priced KFC done properly.

places.ad: 941 Upper Serangoon Road, Singapore 534709
places.w: A corner-kopitiam stall two minutes from Kovan MRT doing all-day Western breakfasts — big brekkies, pancakes, creamy scrambled eggs — at hawker prices from S$3.90. Cafe brunch without the cafe markup.

places.ad: myVillage @ Serangoon Garden, 1 Maju Avenue, #02-07/8/9, Singapore 556679
places.w: A tonkatsu specialist at myVillage by Chef Tan, using Sangenton pork air-flown from Japan, each loin tenderised and breaded only on order for a super-crunchy cutlet. Serangoon Gardens' go-to for premium katsu and ramen.

places.n: Yi Ji Fried Hokkien Prawn Mee
places.ad: 965 Upper Serangoon Road (Mee Sek Food Court), Singapore 534721
places.w: A popular Kovan fried Hokkien prawn mee that has spawned several branches — a spicy, prawn-rich plate with meat and abalone. The Upper Serangoon original anchors the group.

places.ad: Blk 805 Hougang Central, #01-116, Singapore 530805
places.w: A near-20-year Hougang coffeeshop Western stall famous for huge portions at small prices — chicken chop, sirloin, black-pepper lamb, hot-plate mixed grill and fish & chips. Value old-school hawker Western.

places.n: Yi Dian Xin Hong Kong Dim Sum
places.ad: 973 Upper Serangoon Road, Singapore 534725
places.w: An affordable Upper Serangoon dim sum spot near Kovan doing hearty Hong Kong-style plates — signature prawn dumplings and salted-egg custard bao among them. A neighbourhood dim sum fix.

places.ad: 957 Upper Serangoon Road, Singapore 534717
places.w: A pojangmacha-style Korean tent-bar in Kovan — Korean fried chicken, army stew and soju into the small hours. A late-night Korean option on Upper Serangoon Road.

places.ad: Blk 6 Hougang Avenue 3, #01-78, Singapore 530006
places.w: A long-running Hougang cai png shop beloved for very affordable economic rice — fried chicken wings, braised pork, stir-fried veg — from as little as S$2 a plate.

places.n: Mei Xi Hakka Yong Tau Foo
places.ad: Ci Yuan Hawker Centre, 51 Hougang Avenue 9, #01-17, Singapore 538776
places.w: A Ci Yuan stall where the Hakka owner marinates her own fish paste and offers unusual items — fried bean rolls, deep-fried yam strings and egg rolls — alongside the usual yong tau foo pieces.

places.ad: 66A Serangoon Garden Way, Singapore 555962
places.w: A Serangoon Gardens brunch cafe (second outlet after Toa Payoh) celebrated for its egg dishes, mains and desserts in an easy neighbourhood setting.

places.ad: 1014 Upper Serangoon Road, Singapore 534752
places.w: A Western coffeeshop stall hidden in a Kovan kopitiam eight minutes from the MRT, doing generous rosti with oversized pork chops and chargrilled chicken chops at affordable prices.

places.ad: myVillage @ Serangoon Garden, 1 Maju Avenue, #02-10/11, Singapore 556679
places.w: The first yakiniku outlet from the Waa Cow! beef-bowl brand — a grill-it-yourself concept at myVillage with cuts like karubi, oyster blade, striploin and ox tongue plus pork, chicken and veg, from S$4.90.

places.ad: 15 Simon Road, Singapore 545903
places.w: A Simon Road matcha-specialty cafe near Kovan by the team behind Fat Cat Ice Cream Bar — premium Japanese matcha, creative tea drinks, artisan ice cream and a matcha Basque burnt cheesecake that often sells out within hours.

places.ad: Blk 335 Hougang Avenue 7, Singapore 530335
places.w: A cult scrambled-egg-rice stall (高文滑蛋饭) — silky wat-dan-style egg over rice — that outgrew its old Kovan 209 home and relocated to a Hougang Avenue 7 coffeeshop in mid-2024.

places.ad: Hainanese Village Centre, 105 Hougang Avenue 1, #02-04, Singapore 530105
places.w: A 40-year-old Hainanese Village Centre stall, now run by second-gen hawker Nicholas Neo, famous for finger-sized fried carrot cake sticks — crisp outside, tender inside — sold by the thousand daily.

places.ad: Hainanese Village Centre, 105 Hougang Avenue 1, #02-28, Singapore 530105
places.w: A Hainanese Village Centre stall (easy to spot by its fuchsia signboard) plating fragrant coconut rice with crackly-skinned roasted pork belly and crispy ikan bilis — S$3 sets that draw an early crowd.

places.ad: 678 Hougang Avenue 8, #01-505, Singapore 530678
places.w: A family-run old-school bakery in Hougang turning out traditional S$1 cakes and pastries — pandan, kaya, sugar rolls — the kind of heartland bakery that's getting rarer.
